note: Summer 2022 Q5(b) reports errors moving the x terms to one side; Summer 2023 Q7(b) reports errors in rearranging.

label: Undoes a logarithm by dividing or multiplying instead of going to the index form: log to the base x of 216 = 3 answered as 216 divided by 3, or log to the base 4 of x = 3 answered as 4 times 3
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2023 Q7(a) reports candidates unable to build a number from the logarithms they were given; Summer 2019 Q9 reports the index form not being used to undo a logarithm.

label: Exchanges a and d for the inverse but leaves the signs of b and c unchanged
subject: further-maths
note: The same two report blocks as fm.matrix.adjugate-not-swapped: the step is named, the sub-error is not.

label: Negates b and c for the inverse but leaves a and d where they were, instead of exchanging them
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2025 Q5(i) and Summer 2019 Q5 report inverses that were wrong in one step; the reports do not itemise which half of the swap-and-negate rule was dropped, so the evidence is step-level.

label: Writes a pair of simultaneous equations as a matrix equation wrongly: coefficients read down the columns instead of across the rows, constants put in with the coefficients, a missing term's zero left out or written as 1, or a term carried across the equals sign without changing its sign
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2025 Q5(ii) reports that candidates who did use a matrix method struggled with the layout and structure of their working; the report names the layout, not which of these slips caused it.

label: Divides one entry of the adjugate by the determinant and leaves the other three undivided
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2025 Q5(i) reports the factor of 1 over the determinant handled wrongly; which entries it reached is not itemised.

label: Adds the two diagonal products for the determinant, ad + bc, instead of subtracting them
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2019 Q5 reports arithmetic slips in the determinant and Summer 2025 Q5(i) a wrongly handled reciprocal of it; the reports name the wrong determinant, not whether the products were added or subtracted the wrong way round.

label: Works out the determinant as bc - ad instead of ad - bc, so its sign is wrong
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2019 Q5 reports arithmetic slips in the determinant; Summer 2025 Q5(i) reports 1 over 26 written where 1 over minus 26 belonged. The reports name the wrong determinant, not the order it was taken in.

label: Adds or subtracts matrices of different sizes, or multiplies when the first matrix's columns do not match the second's rows
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2023 Q8 reports candidates subtracting matrices of different sizes; Summer 2022 Q3(a)(ii) records confusion about which products are allowed at all.

label: Multiplies two matrices entry by entry in matching positions instead of row by column
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2019 Q1 and Summer 2024 Q7(a)(ii) report each element squared where a matrix product was wanted, which is this rule applied to a matrix by itself; Summer 2023 Q8 reports products that did not even come out 2 by 2.

label: Undoes a matrix in an equation with the wrong operation or in the wrong order: divides by a matrix, subtracts one that is multiplying, uses an inverse where the matrix was only added, uses the matrix itself where its inverse belongs, or reaches for the inverse before an added matrix is cleared
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2018 Q5 credits the candidates who realised that the inverse was central, and Summer 2019 Q5 says most knew they needed the inverse of P; neither report itemises what the others did instead, so the evidence is step-level.

label: Gives the swapped-and-negated matrix as the inverse, with the factor of 1 over the determinant left off altogether
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2025 Q5(i) reports the reciprocal of the determinant written wrongly; Summer 2022 Q3(b) reports determinant slips inside an inverse. Leaving the factor off entirely is the extreme of the same step.

label: Multiplies the inverse on the wrong side (Q P inverse instead of P inverse Q)
subject: further-maths

label: Solves by elimination when the question says to use the matrix method (no marks)
subject: further-maths

label: Has a negative determinant and writes its reciprocal without the minus sign, 1 over 5 where 1 over minus 5 belongs, so every entry of the inverse comes out with the wrong sign
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2025 Q5(i) reports inverses written with 1 over 26 where 1 over minus 26 belonged; the report does not say whether the determinant itself or only its reciprocal lost the sign.

label: Pairs a row of the first matrix with a row of the second (or a column with a column) instead of row by column, so the product's entries land in the wrong places
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2023 Q8 reports a surprising number of products that were not 2 by 2; Summer 2025 Q1 reports sign and position slips inside an otherwise well-done product. The reports name the wrong product, not which pairing produced it.

label: Squares the matrix (or squares each element) instead of multiplying by a scalar or multiplying matrices
subject: further-maths

label: Tries to invert a matrix whose determinant is zero, or cannot say which matrix has no inverse
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2023 Q6(ii) reports that most knew the equation could not be solved but were unclear about which matrix had no inverse.

label: Takes a matrix subtraction the wrong way round, working B - A where A - B was wanted (or rearranging A + X = B as X = A - B), so every entry has the wrong sign
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2018 Q5 reports slips in the P - Q part and Summer 2024 Q7(a) arithmetic errors in B - 2C; neither report itemises a subtraction taken the wrong way round, so the evidence is step-level.

label: Reads the solution column the wrong way round, giving x the bottom entry and y the top, or leaves the column standing as the answer without naming either value
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2025 Q5(ii) reports that candidates who did use a matrix method struggled with the layout of the solution; the report names the layout, not which half of it went wrong.

label: Multiplies a force by its distance from the end of the rod (or from some other point) instead of from the point the moments are taken about, or gives a distance measured from the wrong end
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2023 Q5 and Summer 2024 Q5 record moments taken about A, B, C, D and the centre, with mixed success, and Summer 2022 Q6 records many incorrect moment equations; a distance measured from one point while moments are taken about another is our reading of the commonest way such an equation goes wrong.

label: Uses moments where resolving vertically was needed (or vice versa)
subject: further-maths

label: Takes moments about a point that keeps both unknown reactions in the equation, or about the point where the wanted force acts so that it drops out, instead of about the support whose reaction is not wanted
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2023 Q5 and Summer 2024 Q5 record moments about A, B, C, D and the centre of the rod all being seen; choosing a point that does not remove the unwanted unknown is our reading of why so many of those equations stalled.

label: Mishandles reactions given in a ratio: treats R and 3R as unrelated unknowns, divides by the wrong number of parts, puts the ratio the wrong way round, or uses it in only one of the two equations
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2022 Q6(ii) states that a large number of candidates could not deal with R and 3R, and that a mark was given for three times a calculated reaction.

label: Does not recalculate the reaction when the load changes before taking moments again
subject: further-maths

label: Omits the weight of the rod when taking moments
subject: further-maths

label: Guesses the unknown distance instead of keeping it as a variable in the moments equation
subject: further-maths

label: Uses a resistance given per kilogram as the whole force, without multiplying it by the mass
subject: further-maths

label: Keeps the old mass in F = ma after the load or the body changes, so the new acceleration or force is worked with the mass of an earlier part
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2022 Q3(b)(ii) reports candidates who kept the first box's 6 kg in the equation for the second, 8 kg box.

label: Adds a resistance to the driving force instead of taking it off, so the resultant comes out too large
subject: further-maths
note: The blocks record equations of motion going wrong without itemising the sign; a resistance added rather than subtracted is the commonest form of it.

label: Substitutes one force into F = ma without forming the resultant along the line of motion first
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2025 Q6 records the successful route as identifying the friction and then equating to 7a; substituting a single force instead is our reading of what the rest did.

label: Adds the standard deviations on one side of the mean only, so a range that should be centred on the mean starts or ends at it
subject: further-maths
note: No report names this slip. The source is the Summer 2019 Q5 report's instruction that a good diagram has the mean under the curve's centre with the values marked either side; a range read from such a sketch runs both ways from the mean. The evidence is by analogy and is flagged as such.

label: Cannot handle a negative z-value (leaves 0.8849 where 0.1151 was needed)
subject: further-maths

label: Misreads the 68% and 95% figures of the normal curve: swaps them, gives the band between the mean and one standard deviation where the tail beyond it was asked, or does not halve the share outside between the two tails
subject: further-maths
note: No paper has yet set the proportions as a part of their own, so no report itemises this slip. The source is the Summer 2019 Q5 finding that nearly a fifth of candidates had not met the normal distribution at all (the question left blank or the standard deviation formula tried); the proportions are the first facts such a candidate lacks. The evidence is by analogy and is flagged as such.

label: Attempts a normal-distribution question with the standard deviation formula, or leaves it blank
subject: further-maths

label: Reads the table value but forgets to subtract from 1 for the required tail
subject: further-maths

label: Takes the table value away from 1 when the region wanted is the one the table (or its mirror image) already gives, so a probability of more than a half comes out as less than a half
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2024 Q5(ii) reports the wrong area chosen, 0.0062 given for P(z > -2.5); Summer 2025 Q6(ii) reports 0.0808 given where 0.9192 was needed. Both are the table value subtracted from 1 for a right-hand region above a negative z.

label: Does not know or misuses z = (x - mean) / sd
subject: further-maths

label: Rounds z to one decimal place before reading the Normal Probability Table, so the table value and the answer come out slightly wrong
subject: further-maths
note: No report names this slip in the normal question itself. The source is the Summer 2019 Q4(b)(ii) finding that early rounding cost the final mark in the same paper; rounding z before the table is that habit applied to the table read, so the evidence is by analogy and is flagged as such.

label: Cannot form the constraint (e.g. L = x + 2y) from the diagram
subject: further-maths

label: Leaves area or perimeter expressions unsimplified, causing later algebraic slips
subject: further-maths

label: Stops at the value of x instead of substituting to find the quantity the question asked for
subject: further-maths

label: Does not use the second derivative (or another test) to show the stationary value is a maximum or minimum
subject: further-maths

label: Reaches x squared = k when the derivative is set to zero and gives k as the answer, leaving the square root untaken
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2022 Q13 reports a derivative of the form -900/x squared being treated as x squared = 900, which is this step left unfinished; Summer 2025 Q14(iii) reports difficulty solving the equation that follows a negative power.

label: Reaches the optimised quantity and writes the bare number on the answer line, with no unit
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2022 Q13 reports the wrong quantity given on the answer line and Summer 2019 Q14 reports unfinished final steps; the missing unit is the presentational half of that, and is our reading.

label: Counts a side that a wall, hedge or river already provides, so the constraint fences four sides instead of three
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2022 Q13 reports many candidates unable to read the constraint from the diagram; the particular miscount is our reading of the commonest wrong constraint.

label: Answers produced on a calculator with no method shown, earning nothing
subject: further-maths

label: Adds probabilities of successive events instead of multiplying
subject: further-maths

label: Counts one order of a two-event outcome, not both
subject: further-maths

label: Adds every qualifying branch instead of taking the complement from 1, or gives the complement's probability as the answer
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2024 Q3(ii)(b) says candidates who calculated all six probabilities made extra work and sometimes an error where subtracting from 1 was simpler; Summer 2025 Q7(ii) uses the same complement step.

label: Converts exact fraction probabilities to rounded decimals part-way through and loses accuracy
subject: further-maths

label: Takes P(A and B) as P(A) times P(B) when nothing says the two events are independent, or treats mutually exclusive events as independent
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2022 Q7(iii) and Summer 2023 Q5(iii) report most candidates multiplying two probabilities for the intersection of two events that were not independent (there one lay inside the other, which fm.condprob.subset-event-multiplied records); using P(A) times P(B) as the overlap in the addition rule, or taking it off for mutually exclusive events, is the same assumption on a different question.

label: Multiplies P(BB) and P(GG) instead of adding them
subject: further-maths

label: Misreads 'only' so the overlaps are placed wrongly, or omits the region outside the circles
subject: further-maths

label: Multiplies the two probabilities for an 'or' event instead of adding them and taking off the overlap
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2024 Q3(i) reports a one-mark part read as an 'and' question, two probabilities multiplied (5/44 for 5/11) where no 'and' was asked; Summer 2022 Q1 reports the mirror-image swap, adding where 'and' needed multiplying. Neither was an 'or' question, so the evidence for this exact slip is step-level: the add-or-multiply decision made the wrong way.

label: Adds P(A) and P(B) for an 'or' event and never takes the intersection off, so everybody in both is counted twice and the answer can exceed 1
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2019 Q7(i) reports answers greater than 1 and regions not added before dividing, which is this rule half-applied. Summer 2024 Q3 is a tree whose parts add branch probabilities; its report names arithmetic errors there without itemising a double-counted overlap, so the evidence is step-level.

label: Leaves the denominator unchanged on the second or third draw of a without-replacement tree, as if the first item had gone back
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2024 Q3(ii) reports a minority of candidates working with replacement throughout; Summer 2019 Q2 is the same without-replacement structure.

label: Gives a count (10) or a count over the whole population where a probability of the reduced group was wanted
subject: further-maths

label: Fills a Venn diagram without checking the numbers total the stated population
subject: further-maths

label: Ignores a constant on the other side of a quadratic inequality and solves the wrong quadratic
subject: further-maths

label: Includes negative or impossible values in a context that excludes them
subject: further-maths

label: Draws the wrong graph when the x squared coefficient is negative
subject: further-maths

label: Picks the wrong region because no sketch of the quadratic was drawn
subject: further-maths

label: Treats the inequality as an equation throughout and loses the sign
subject: further-maths

label: Adds or removes values from the sum of squares without squaring them
subject: further-maths

label: Combines two groups by averaging their means instead of using the totals
subject: further-maths

label: Combines two groups by averaging their standard deviations, or by subtracting one from the other, instead of rebuilding the sums of squares
subject: further-maths
note: The reports name the averaging habit on the two means and record the pooled standard deviation being done well or not at all; applying the same habit to the two standard deviations is our reading of the second half.

label: Divides the fx total by the number of classes instead of by the total frequency

label: Gets the direction wrong when saying how an added, removed or corrected value moves the mean or the standard deviation

label: Rounds a mean to a whole number or gives answers not to 2 decimal places

label: Roots the sum of squares over n without subtracting the mean squared, so the answer measures the size of the data rather than its spread
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2025 Q2 records sums put into the standard-deviation formula in the wrong place; which term was dropped is our reading.

label: Represents a class by one of its limits, or by its width, instead of by its midpoint
subject: further-maths
note: The blocks cited record marks lost inside the grouped table; the particular column that was wrong is our reading.

label: Uses the original mean with the adjusted sum of squares, so the spread is measured about the wrong centre
subject: further-maths

label: Adjusts a total with only one of the two values in a correction, so an item is double-counted or lost
subject: further-maths

label: Uses the calculator's s, which divides by n minus 1, where this specification's sigma divides by n
subject: further-maths
note: No report names the divisor explicitly; the blocks cited are the ones recording the standard-deviation calculation going wrong, and this is the calculator slip a learner makes most easily.

label: Confuses (sum of x) squared with sum of x squared, or squares the fx column instead of f times x squared
subject: further-maths

label: Treats a table of daily values as a grouped frequency table and invents midpoints

label: Reaches a group's sum of squares and then does not divide it by that group's own n before subtracting the mean squared

label: Adds a constant to the standard deviation when a constant is added to every value

label: Finds the added constant from the two standard deviations, which never contain it, instead of from the two means

note: Summer 2023 Q6 reports strange equations in the two unknowns when the scaling was worked backwards; an equation for the constant built from the standard deviations is our reading of one of them.

label: Carries a negative scale factor's minus sign into the standard deviation, giving a negative spread
subject: further-maths
note: Summer 2023 Q6 records the scaling step failing for nearly half the candidates without itemising the sign; the negative spread is our reading of one way it fails.

label: Leaves the standard deviation as it was when every value is multiplied by a scale factor, so only the mean is transformed

note: Summer 2023 Q6 reports just over half handling the scaling in full and Summer 2024 Q1 names the standard deviation being moved wrongly under a shift; neither itemises an unscaled standard deviation, so the evidence is step-level.

subject: further-maths
note: The reports record the standard-deviation step failing after the mean was found (Summer 2023 Q6: about 30% earned only the mark for the mean) without naming which sub-step was dropped; the missing square root is our reading of that.

label: Recovers a group's sum of squares as n times the mean squared, dropping the sigma squared term that carries the spread

label: Answers for the group that was subtracted away, or for the group the question already described, rather than for the one it names
subject: further-maths

label: Uses the old n (14 instead of 15) after adding a value
subject: further-maths

label: Uses a value printed in a later part (a 'show that' result) to answer an earlier part, which scores nothing

label: Solves the two-unknown pair and never goes back to an original equation for the third value

label: Accepts very large, negative or fractional answers that make no sense in context

label: Writes the three values on the wrong labelled answer lines

label: Starts from the printed equation and works back to the information

label: Writes an equation that does not match the sentence (e.g. x + y - z = 55, or '8 dearer' and '50% greater' mistranslated)

note: Summer 2022 Q10(i) reports derivatives written without knowing what to do next, and Summer 2019 Q8(ii) reports incomplete turning-point work; the dropped second root is our reading.
